row.claim: Against t9-s20919936-d1053205 the latest accepted net scores 296.5/400 = 0.74125 (282 W, 89 L, 29 D), se = sqrt(p(1-p)/n) = 0.021897, 95 % CI [0.6983, 0.7842], Elo +182.8 with 95 % CI [+145.8, +224.1]; the exact Clopper-Pearson interval over the 371 decisive games is [0.7133, 0.8027], Elo [+158.4, +243.7]. Against t9-s143744-d157367 it scores 400/400; the normal interval is degenerate there (se = 0) and the exact 95 % interval is [0.9908, 1.0000], i.e. Elo > +813. Colours are balanced by construction, 200 games of each per arm, and the split is 135/200 = 0.6750 [0.6101, 0.7399] as Black and 161.5/200 = 0.8075 [0.7529, 0.8621] as White in arm A. Therefore, at the gate's visit count, the 19-export stall in p0loss (best 1.485115) and pacc1 (best 0.544882) is a stall of those two metrics and NOT of playing strength: the run gained about 183 Elo over the net that still holds both records. By the memo's pre-registered rule (p >= 0.60), option (b), LR x0.5, is NOT triggered for link 4

assumptions: one .sgfs line is one game (the same rule match.sbatch:142 counts by); 400 lines were written per arm and none carried a board size other than SZ[9]
a draw scores 0.5 to each side, matching drawEquivalentWinsForWhite = 0.5 in both the match and the selfplay configs

the normal-approximation CI treats the SCORE as a binomial proportion although 29 of arm A's 400 games are draws; the exact Clopper-Pearson interval quoted alongside it is computed on the 371 decisive games only, and the two agree to within 0.015 in p
Elo is the logistic map -400 log10(1/p - 1), the same convention DESIGN section 7 uses; it is a summary of p at these visits and is not claimed to transfer to other search budgets
the snapshot BASEDIR held byte-identical copies of the three nets (sha256 verified against runs/p1 before the job and re-verified inside it)

row.notes: The number that answers the memo's question 2 is 0.7412 with a 95 % CI whose lower end, 0.6983, is still far above the 0.60 decision line, so the rule discharges cleanly in the do-nothing direction. The colour split is reported because it is the only place a pairing bug would show: at komi 7 White scores 0.5663 [0.5178, 0.6148] pooled over both bots in arm A, a real but symmetric edge that cancels from the head-to-head number because each net plays exactly 200 games of each colour.
